current.text: Charlotte got him from Minnesota in the LaMelo Ball trade.
He is projected to start at power forward, in the spot Miles Bridges left. Diabaté is the projected starting center.
Experts expect the most minutes of his career, about 31 to 33 per game. He may play more power forward than center.
Diabaté, Kalkbrenner and Kai Jones limit his minutes at center.
With LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges gone, Charlotte has a lot of open usage. His usage is projected to rise from about 22 to about 24.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes. Playmaking will be spread across several players.
The newest preview calls him a strong mid-round target in the 55 to 75 range and says he goes earlier in category leagues.

Experts disagree on his upside. Some say he has a better chance of making the top 50 than of falling outside the top 100. Others put him in tier seven with no upside beyond that and say he is not as good as the hype.
Do not pay for a top 30 per game rank.
In a recent mock auction he went for 14 USD. The drafter had hoped to get him for about 10 USD.
With a March 28 end, Charlotte plays 4, 3 and 4 games in the playoff weeks. The team has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte has only two games in the week starting March 1.

durable.text: He makes many threes for a forward or center and adds useful blocks. FG% is his weakest category for his position, but the code does not flag it as weak.
He is a very good floor spacer who can play the four or the five.
He is a bad defender. His shooting is up and down, and he can be an inefficient scorer.
He is not a strong fantasy center. He does not boost FG% or bring big rebound numbers.
He has not yet shown he can handle a big usage load. One expert calls him a backup on a good team and a starter on a bad one.

note: Market prices are low: 4.1 USD average cost on Yahoo, 10 USD on ESPN, and 2 USD in our league last season. In a recent mock auction he went for 14 USD, so a 10 to 14 USD bid fits the 55 to 75 rank range experts give him. He suits most builds, mainly teams that want threes and blocks from a big, but he will not help FG% on about 13 shots a game. Early in the season, check that he plays 31 or more minutes as a starter, how much center time he gets next to Diabaté, and whether his FG% holds at 45 or better with the higher usage.
